newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close mixed after triple-witching.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close mixed after triple-witching.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended mixed in brisk dealings on Friday, amid quarterly triple-witching and nervousness over a possible U.S. interest rate hike.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 19.50 points to 6074.78 on turnover of 101.5 million shares worth C$1.9 billion.
Today's early volatility was due partly to the quarterly expiry of options, futures and options on futures called triple-witching, traders said.
Investors were also waiting to see if rates were hiked at next Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"We have the anticipation of (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan doing what he said he was going to do," said Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones 491 to 447 while another 331 traded unchanged.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, ten strengthened including banks, oils, forestry products and conglomerates. The weaker side was led by golds and base metals.
During the week, Canada's largest equities exchange lost 87 points from its open of 6161.13 on Monday.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd topped Toronto's most actives, sinking 2.25 to 15.20 on more than nine million shares. Bre-X said partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc had not completed its due diligence after a report cast doubt on the size of the rich Busang gold discovery.

* Sofware maker Cognos Inc jumped 4.10 to 33.10 in moderate trading after UBS Securities upgraded it to strong buy from hold. The brokerage also raised yearly earnings estimate to $1.10 from $1.04 for fiscal 1998 which ends in February.
